name: Disseminated Superficial Actinic Porokeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for DSAP

criteria.description: Presence of multiple annular, keratotic, atrophic plaques with raised hyperkeratotic borders predominantly on sun-exposed skin
Histological identification of cornoid lamellae in skin biopsy specimens
Lesions predominantly located on sun-exposed areas such as forearms and legs
Positive family history of porokeratosis or similar lesions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions with histopathological confirmation of cornoid lamellae
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by biopsy; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

other: Skin biopsy showing cornoid lamellae is diagnostic

distinguishingFeatures: Typically solitary or few larger plaques
Lesions often on trunk and extremities but less sun-exposed
Earlier onset in childhood or adolescence
Rough, scaly patches rather than annular plaques
Higher risk of progression to squamous cell carcinoma

redFlags: Rapid enlargement or ulceration of lesions indicating possible malignancy
Development of nodular or verrucous changes within plaques
New onset of pain or bleeding from lesions
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2020.
Sun JD, et al. Genetic basis of disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis: a review. J Dermatol Sci. 2021;101(1):2-9.
